content:
olivia_support: Heads-up — ACME reports a behavior regression after yesterday's rollout. Their prompt now produces truncated IDs and different phrasing. They suspect tokenizer/segmentation changes. Repro + logs below.

olivia_support: Repro payload (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions 
  -H '\"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\"' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-medium-v1\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful assistant.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Summarize order ID: 6421-ABCD-9000 for the payments ledger.\"}],\"max_tokens\":120}'
```

olivia_support: Expected (pre-rollout):
```
Assistant: Order 6421-ABCD-9000: paid on 2026-02-03, amount $1,240. Next step: reconcile with ledger entry #9000.
```

olivia_support: After rollout (customer):
```
Assistant: Order 6421-AB C D 9000: paid 02/03, amount $1,240. Reconcile ledger.
```

joe_eng: Which exact runtime/config was deployed? any deploy id or flag changed? :eyes:

olivia_support: Model=redwood-medium-v1, API path /v1/chat/completions. Ops flipped a segmentation flag in the tokenizer layer during the rollout: `segmentation_mode=aggressive`. Deploy-bot posted a deploy at ~1849987600.

deploy-bot: Deployed segmentation_mode=aggressive to service=inference-1 at 1849987600 (deploy id=deploy-2026-02-12-09).

sam_runtime: I tried the same payload locally with segmentation_mode=aggressive and can reproduce the spacing in token boundaries. Looks like the pre-token whitespace normalization changed — some hyphenated/alphanumeric groups are being split into extra sub-tokens. Quick token debug dump: 
```
input: "6421-ABCD-9000"
legacy tokens: ["6421","-ABCD-","9000"]
aggressive tokens: ["6421","-","AB","CD","-","9000"]
```

maria_ml: That matches PR #3456 where we updated the default byte-level splitter to improve mixed-language handling. It unintentionally changed the default split rules for alphanumeric-hyphen groups. The PR note mentioned whitespace normalization but we missed this edge case.

ben_support: Customer is anxious, asking if this will change how their downstream parsing works. Can we offer a rollback or a per-tenant fallback?

acme_prod: Confirming, we started seeing this at 2026-02-12T11:22:13-08:00. Our parsers treat hyphen groups as single tokens, so this split breaks our regex. Happy to provide more samples.

lisa_security: Any sensitive data in logs? if we do rollback or capture more traces, ensure we mask PII.

sam_runtime: Mitigation plan: 1) add a routing override so ACME traffic uses `segmentation_mode=legacy` (pin to previous tokenizer) 2) hotfix PR to adjust the splitter rules and tests 3) small canary rollback if hotfix will take >2h. I can push the route override now.

olivia_support: OK proceeding with routing override and asking SRE for a canary rollback window. @oncall-bot please create an incident and mark P1 if customer impact > 1 tenant.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-324 — title: tokenization-segmentation-regression (P1 candidate). Assigned to eng-runtime.

maria_ml: I'll revert the splitter change branch locally and create unit tests covering hyphenated alphanumeric groups. We'll coordinate with runtime for a staged deploy.

ben_support: I'll update the customer: temporary fallback applied, working on a long-term fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
